language-family.def: A group of languages that grew from one ancient ancestor language. Indo-European, which includes English, Spanish and Hindi, is one.

dialect.def: A regional version of one language, with its own words, pronunciation or grammar, that speakers of other versions can still mostly understand.

toponym.def: A place name. Toponyms often record who named or settled a place, such as the Spanish names of Santa Fe and Los Angeles.

universalizing-religion.def: A religion that seeks followers from any place or group and spreads widely. AP® Human Geography classes Christianity, Islam, Buddhism and Sikhism this way.

ethnic-religion.def: A religion tied to one people and their homeland, which mostly stays near its hearth or spreads when followers migrate. AP® Human Geography classes Hinduism and Judaism this way.
